The fed funds rate is around 1.16%, which fits mid-to-late 2017: the Fed raised rates in June 2017 to a 1.00-1.25% range, so the effective rate would be about 1.16%.

The unemployment rate is 4.3%, which matches mid-2017 (May-July 2017 was 4.3-4.4%). The 10-year yield is 2.15%, and the 2-year is 1.33%, which suggests around August 2017, though the 2-year was 1.38% in August and 1.33% in July. Headline CPI of 1.73% year over year fits July 2017 (1.7%), and core CPI of 1.7% also matches July (1.7%). Gold rose 4.5% in the month, which fits August 2017 (gold jumped from about 1268 to 1320), while July gold gained about 2%. The 10-year yield at 2.15% fits end of August, when it was about 2.12%. The 20+ year Treasury gain of 2.6% in the month also fits August. US equity returned 0.0% in August 2017 (S&P up 0.1%), and VIX at 11.22 doesn't quite fit the end of August (VIX was about 10.6), but a 12-month-ago comparison is hard to settle. The 3-month change in headline CPI of -0.47 fits as well, since CPI was 2.7% in February 2017 and 1.7% in July or August. Payrolls averaged about 195k, which matches data known at the end of August.

I'm choosing August 2017.
